items.why: The report says the "D band grows strongly with dose while G stays put, and the D and G linewidths stay narrow in doses 1–3. This is stage-1". It gives G FWHM of about 14 cm^-1 and 2D FWHM of about 32 cm^-1 with I(2D)/I(G) of about 3, and reports D' heights rising from 111 to 340 to 436.
By height it gives I(D)/I(G) of 0.253, 0.577 and 1.188, and "Height ratios give 23.9, 15.8 and 11.0 nm". All three L_D values fall within the rubric ranges, and the method is Cançado Eq. 4.

It explicitly uses "L_D^2 = 1.8e-9 · λ^4 / (I_D/I_G), with λ = 532 nm (prefactor ≈ 144 nm^2)", which is the wavelength-dependent form. It also notes the numbers "assume ... the 532 nm excitation" and asks for a second laser line to check the "λ^-4 scaling".

It says dose 4 is "stage 2" with a broad G that is "really G+D' merged", the "2D band nearly vanishes", L_D ≲ 3 nm, and "The Cançado L_D formula does not apply there". It also warns that reading I(D)/I(G) alone "would wrongly conclude dose 4 is less damaged".

It reports "I(D)/I(D') ... ≈6.4, 6.1, 6.8 ... By area: 6.9, 7.6, 7.6" and cites Eckmann 2012: "~3.5 for boundaries, ~7 for vacancy-like defects and ~13 for sp3-type". The ratio is applied only to the stage-1 doses 1–3.

It clearly reports both height and area ratios and says the summary values are "(areas)", noting that height values are "within about 3%". It never says that Cançado's relation is calibrated on peak heights, and its headline numbers use areas.

It asks "What was the treatment (Ar+ ion, O2/H2 plasma, electron beam, irradiation, chemical)...? Without this I cannot validate the calibration". It also notes that the calibration was done with Ar+ point defects and that hydrogenation would change I_D/I_D' (~13).

wrong_claims.why: It concludes that dose 4 has a higher density (n_D ≳ 3.5e12 cm^-2, L_D ≲ 3 nm) and explicitly rejects the idea that dose 4 is less damaged.
It uses λ = 532 nm in the λ^4 formula, not the 514.5 nm constants.
It identifies "a sharp single-point cosmic-ray spike near ~2150 cm^-1 in dose 2" as an artefact and excludes it from the fits.

items.why: The report says "Both G and 2D red-shift monotonically with laser power", that linewidths grow ("G FWHM 13.8 → 15.7 → 17.9"), that the Si line holds at 520.86–520.91 cm-1, and concludes the shifts are "almost certainly laser heating".

It uses χG ≈ −0.016 cm-1/K but only gives "of order 100 K at 5 mW (about 25 K/mW)", which is below the rubric's ~125 K; it never states a 2 mW value and declines to cross-check with the 2D coefficient.
It reports Δ2D/ΔG ≈ 2.8 "against the strain-line slope of about 2.2" from Lee et al. and warns that plotting the 2 and 5 mW points "would wrongly suggest growing tensile strain".
It says to "Use the 0.5 mW spectrum, or better a power series extrapolated to zero power, for strain/doping analysis. Treat 2 and 5 mW as heated."

It asks for "the objective/spot size (NA)" to get power density, and asks the user to "record at 0.1–0.25 mW ... and extrapolate the peak positions to zero power" to check that the lowest power is free of heating.
It takes the 0.5 mW spectrum (G = 1581.3, 2D = 2669.5) as the reference and finds it "on or near the origin within a few cm-1" after a 532 nm dispersion correction of 2D that it marks as uncertain.

wrong_claims.why: The report rejects strain or doping as the cause ("not a different strain or doping state of the flake"; "A doping change is not supported").
It recommends the lowest-power spectrum, "0.5 mW (lowest heating)", not the highest-power one.

items.why: The report states "Both spectra contain the graphene D, G and 2D bands". It gives G at 1580.4/1581 and 2D at 2681.3/2696–2698 cm⁻¹ and concludes "Yes, both spectra show graphene".

The report gives D at 1344.3 (Au) and 1348 (Cu) cm⁻¹, with "I_D/I_G is 111/116 = 0.96 on Au ... and 13/24 = 0.55 on Cu". It adds that the Cu value is uncertain because the D band is only about 1.5× the noise.

The report never links the stronger D on Au to strain from rapid solidification. It attributes the Au D to "high ethylene flux and fast growth, which would give many nuclei and many grain boundaries" and uses strain only to explain the 2D shift on Cu.

The report states "Edges, grain boundaries, sp³ sites and vacancies all give D intensity". It also tests its strain explanation against the G and 2D shifts: "A 16 cm⁻¹ shift from strain alone would then give a G shift of roughly +6 to +7 cm⁻¹, which the data disfavour".

The report asks "What was the laser wavelength?" and says it is needed for the absolute D and 2D positions and for the L_D conversion. The caveats add that "2D ~100 cm⁻¹/eV, and I_D/I_G scales as λ⁻⁴".
The caveats say "The Cu spectrum is noisy ... so the Cu D/G ratio, D width and any D' are poorly determined", and the report quotes error bars for the Cu fits.

wrong_claims.why: The report gives "L_D ≈ 12 nm" on Au and "≈ 16 nm" on Cu based on an assumed 532 nm wavelength. It calls the values indicative, but it still states quantitative L_D values without knowing the wavelength.
The report never says strain causes the D peak on Au. It attributes the Au defects tentatively to growth conditions and treats strain as a hypothesis for the Cu 2D shift.

items.why: The report states the E2g band of flake 2 "is blue-shifted by 2.8 ± 0.3 cm-1 (1368.99 vs 1366.19) and ~20% broader" and calls this "compatible with a monolayer or few-layer hBN".
It says position alone is not conclusive ("the magnitude is small and disputed", "Raman alone cannot establish it is a monolayer") but never mentions the ~±2 cm-1 sample-to-sample variation.

It says the shift is "comparable to strain/substrate effects" and gives compressive strain as one possible cause, but it does not mention red shifts of 1–2 cm-1 from random cleavage strain, or that this strain dominates in bilayers.

It says the ~10x weaker E2g area under the same conditions means flake 2 "is much thinner", and notes that "the E2g intensity scales with layer number but there is no calibration", which covers proportionality once calibrated.

It asks for AFM ("the decisive test") and calibration against a known 1L/2L flake, but it rejects normalising to the Si line ("unreliable") and does not propose optical contrast at a better-suited oxide thickness.

wrong_claims.why: The report repeatedly says monolayer status is "not established" and that Raman "cannot establish it is a monolayer".
The report never says a bilayer is upshifted; it only says 1 to a few layers "cannot be separated".

items.why: The report says "Both MoS2 modes sit about 2.5 cm-1 higher on day 2" (E2g Δ+2.51, A1g Δ+2.44) and that the separation is unchanged (21.57 vs 21.52 cm-1), which is close to the rubric's ~21.4.

It reports "Si 519.98 → 522.47 (Δ+2.49)" and concludes that "A rigid shift of the whole spectrum is a spectrometer calibration offset... Strain or doping in the MoS2 cannot move the Si substrate line."
After referencing to Si it gives "E2g 384.05 vs 384.07 and A1g 405.63 vs 405.58 cm-1", and it says the ~21.5 cm-1 separation "is consistent with a thin flake of about 2 layers" on both days.

It states "Electron doping would soften and broaden A1g much more than E2g, and strain would shift E2g much more strongly than A1g", gives unchanged widths (A1g FWHM 6.4 → 6.4), and reports a differential shift of −0.07±0.12 cm-1.
It asks "Was the spectrometer recalibrated, or the grating or centre wavelength moved, between the two days?" and whether a Si or lamp reference was measured on both days.

wrong_claims.why: It explicitly rejects this: the shift is "not strain or doping" and gives "no evidence of adsorbate doping or strain."
It states "the thickness did not change between days" and finds no defect features on either day.

items.why: The report states "E¹₂g softening and A₁g stiffening" with thickness and lists the values going B → A → D → C, so the separation clearly grows with layer number.

It assigns B as 1L (19.2 cm⁻¹) and A as 2L (21.5 cm⁻¹), matching the rubric numbers, but it does not call the 1L→2L step the most robust distinction; it calls the 2.3 cm⁻¹ difference "not unambiguous on its own".

It gives D at 24.3 cm⁻¹ ("'thicker than 4L' as the firm statement") and C at 25.1 cm⁻¹ as bulk-like, and says "the separation saturates above about 4–5 layers, so D and C cannot be given a layer number".

It says "Absolute intensities are not comparable between spectra" and cites SiO2 interference, but it does not describe the rise-to-~4L-then-fall behaviour, and it uses E¹₂g area as support ("about 2.1× that of B, as expected for 2L vs 1L").

It states that strain mainly shifts E¹₂g and doping mainly shifts A₁g, and that "Either could mimic a one-layer error in the separation"; it also cites A₁g softening and broadening with electron doping (the strain number given is for biaxial, not uniaxial, strain).
It reports A₁g FWHM of 6.6, 5.4 and 4.6 cm⁻¹ for A, B and D against 3.1 cm⁻¹ for C (largest for bilayer A), while E¹₂g FWHM is "2.0–2.2 cm⁻¹ for all four flakes".
It checks calibration against the Si line: "The Si line sits at 519.99–520.04 cm⁻¹ in A, B and D, which also confirms the calibration".

wrong_claims.why: Layer numbers come from the mode separation; intensity and Si attenuation are used only as cross-checks.
It correctly states that E¹₂g softens and the separation grows with thickness.
It calls the 265.1 cm⁻¹ feature "a cosmic-ray spike, not a Raman mode" and excludes it from the fits.

items.why: The report fits the band as two components, "2LA 351.1±0.1 (FWHM 9.0), E' 355.3±0.1 (FWHM 3.9)", and notes that the 351 band is "asymmetric on the high-energy side, which is the buried E'".

It gives "2LA/A1' ~2.2 by peak height" at spot 1 and "~0.7 by height" at spot 2, calls this "the strongest monolayer indicator at this wavelength" and notes a "~5-fold drop in the area ratio"; the thick-spot value of 0.7 is reasonably close to the rubric's ~0.5.
It reports "A1g 417.28 → 420.08 cm-1 (+2.80)" and links spot 1 to a monolayer and spot 2 to bulk-like WS2.
It reports an "A1g–E spacing 62.0 → 64.7 cm-1", using the E' position from the two-component fit that separates it from 2LA(M).

It says positions "distinguish 1L from bulk well but do not cleanly separate 1L from 2L" and that spot 2 cannot be given a thickness "beyond 'bulk-like'", but it never states that the 2L/3L/bulk steps are only ~1 cm-1, so the point is made only partly.

It checks the Si line ("Si 520.9 ... and 520.8 cm-1 ... so the calibration is good") and warns that "The 2LA(M) intensity is strongly resonance-dependent" and that the ratios are "valid only for this laser line".

wrong_claims.why: It assigns the ~351 maximum in spot 1 to 2LA(M) and takes the spacing from the fitted E' at 355.3, not from the band maximum.
It calls 2LA(M) "the 2LA(M) second-order band", says it is resonantly enhanced, and reports "no broad D-like band".

items.why: The report says D grows over doses 1–3 while "G stays narrow (about 14 cm^-1), which places these spectra in stage 1". It also reports D' heights rising (116/331/432) and the 2D band remaining "a single band" that is only slightly broader.
Height ratios 0.249/0.569/1.191 give "L_D 24.1 ± 3.3 nm ... 15.9 ± 2.2 nm ... 11.0 ± 1.5 nm" using Cancado at 532 nm, and all three values fall within the rubric ranges.

The report applies the relation explicitly at "laser 532 nm" and notes that the constant was calibrated at 514.5/632.8/785 nm, with "The lambda^4 scaling" applied. It does not explicitly say that the same ratio maps to a different L_D at another laser line.

The report says dose 4 has "I_D/I_G = 0.57 ... lower than dose 3 even though the damage is larger", with broadened G+D', the 2D band "nearly gone" and the stage 2 regime reached. It concludes that "the L_D relation does not apply" and gives L_D ≲ 3 nm.

The report gives "I_D/I_D' = 6.0 ... 6.2 ... 6.9" and calls this "closer to vacancy-type defects than to sp3 (about 13) or boundaries (about 3.5)". It also states that the ratio is "only valid in stage 1".

The report says it uses height ratios and lists the area ratios (0.26/0.60/1.26) alongside them. It does not say that Cancado's relation is calibrated on heights, or that area ratios differ because the band widths differ.
The report asks "What is the treatment (Ar+ sputtering, O2 plasma, e-beam, irradiation, hydrogenation)... Needed to identify defect type", and elsewhere notes that the relation assumes point defects.

wrong_claims.why: The report states that dose 4 is the most damaged, with L_D ≲ 3 nm, and does not apply Eq. 4 to it.
L_D is computed at 532 nm with lambda^4 scaling, not with the 514.5 nm constants.
The report says the "Spike at 2154.1 cm^-1 in dose 2 was removed (cosmic ray, artifact)".

items.why: The report says "G and 2D downshift and broaden with laser power; this is laser heating" and "Si is stable to 0.05 cm-1, so it is not calibration," with monotonic positions and FWHMs listed for all three powers.
It uses -0.016 cm-1/K to get "about 116 K from G" at 5 mW, and gives a 2D estimate of 151 K, which it calls consistent "within about 30%"; it never states the ~50 K rise at 2 mW.

It reports "Delta2D/DeltaG = 2.8 ± 0.2", says "The strain slope 2.2 ± 0.2 is close" and "the heating slope is about 2.1 from Calizo", and concludes "Strain cannot be separated from heating by slope alone."

It says to "Trust the 0.5 mW spectrum for strain and doping, as an upper bound on the cold position, and do not use the 5 mW one," notes that "heating contaminates all three spectra," and names a power series extrapolated to zero as an option.

It asks "Is the stated power measured at the sample, and what is the spot size?" and warns that "Even 0.5 mW is probably somewhat heated," but it does not recommend measuring at an extra, lower power to confirm the heating-free regime (its suggested 0.5 mW repeat tests reversibility).
It uses the 0.5 mW spectrum (G 1581.14, 2D 2669.3 cm-1) as the reference and finds it "near-neutral, nearly strain-free," with the 2D wavelength correction "uncertain by about 3 cm-1."

wrong_claims.why: It explicitly rejects this: "The G and 2D differences are laser heating, not a change in strain or doping."
It recommends the 0.5 mW spectrum and says "do not use the 5 mW one."

items.why: The report says "Both spectra show graphene G (about 1580 cm-1) and 2D (2681 cm-1 on Au, 2696 cm-1 on Cu), so graphene is present on both metals."

It gives D at 1344.2 cm-1 on Au with "I(D)/I(G) (heights) = 0.97 ± 0.09", and on Cu "I(D)/I(G) = 0.6 ± 0.2" with D "only a weak, low-confidence feature", which matches the rubric numbers and the poor constraint.

It says only in general terms that "Strain frozen in by fast cooling is a plausible contributor" and that "liquid-to-solid change on solidification adds strain"; it never ties this to the stronger D band on Au or presents it as the authors' hypothesis.

It reads the strong D as a sign of defects ("likely higher defect density on Au") and tests strain against the G and 2D shifts using the Lee 2012 slope, but it never states that D needs defects or edges to be activated, or that strain alone cannot produce D.

It asks "What was the laser wavelength?" and explains that "I(D)/I(G) scales with lambda^4" and that D and 2D "disperse with excitation energy (about 52 and 100 cm-1/eV)", so L_D and the positions cannot be compared without it.
It warns that "The Cu spectrum is low signal-to-noise... G, D and their ratios on Cu have errors of 20-35 %, and the G width is essentially unconstrained", and quotes errors throughout.

wrong_claims.why: It explicitly declines: "L_D_nm: Not computed. The relation needs the laser wavelength, which is not recorded."
It never says strain causes the Au D peak; it says "No mechanism is proven by these data" and calls strain only "a plausible contributor".

items.why: The report gives flake 1 E2g at "1366.0" and flake 2 at "1368.84", an upshift of "+2.85 ± 0.25 cm-1". It notes broadening ("FWHM 18.8 ± 0.8 vs 15.5 ± 0.2") and says this fits "a thin, substrate-supported flake (1L or 2L)".
It cites "1L upshifted by typically 2-4 cm-1 (± 2)" and states "Position alone is not a layer-number criterion" and "Position-based layer assignment is unreliable".

It says "position is strain-dependent", mentions "random strain" via Gorbachev, and gives the 2L downshift of 1-2 cm-1. It never states that random strain from cleavage produces red shifts of about 1-2 cm-1, comparable in size to the monolayer upshift.

It reports flake 2's E2g as "about 12x weaker in peak height (about 10x in area)" under identical settings. It calls intensity "the better layer-number observable" and states "integrated E2g is proportional to N for the first few layers on a given substrate, but only after calibration".

It asks for AFM and for optical contrast ("green channel at about 530 nm" on 290 nm SiO2). It also requests a bare-Si spectrum so the Si-line intensity can serve as a reference, alongside an intensity calibration on the same stack.

wrong_claims.why: The report explicitly says "Raman cannot establish that flake 2 is a monolayer" and calls it "1L possible but unproven".

Following Cai, the summary asserts that the upshift "is the pattern reported for supported 1L/2L hBN" and that "1L and 2L are both compatible with 1368.8", treating 2L as upshifted. It does note that Gorbachev's 2L downshift "weighs against 2L".

items.why: The report gives "E2g1 383.33 (day 1) vs 385.83 (day 2), +2.50 cm-1; A1g 404.88 vs 407.31, +2.43 cm-1" and an unchanged separation "Delta = 21.56 ± 0.07 (day 1) and 21.47 ± 0.11 (day 2)".
It states "Si 519.98 vs 522.47, +2.49 cm-1", calls this "a spectrometer calibration drift and not a sample change", and treats Si as the fixed reference at 520.7 cm-1.
After Si referencing, "E2g1 and A1g agree within 0.02 ± 0.03 and -0.07 ± 0.12 cm-1", and the separation of "21.5 ± 0.1 cm-1, consistent with about 2L" holds on both days.

It says "There is no broadening of A1g, which is the usual signature of doping, and no splitting or broadening of E2g1, which would indicate strain", cites A1g softening and broadening under electron doping and -4.5 cm-1/% for E2g1 under strain, and reports unchanged widths.
It asks "Was the spectrometer recalibrated or the grating moved between days? ... Did you record a Si or Ne reference on each day?"

wrong_claims.why: The report rejects the idea outright: "The data give no sign of adsorbate-induced doping or strain."
It says "the layer number is the same" and "Crystal quality has not degraded."

items.why: The report says "The E2g1 softens and the A1g stiffens from 1L to bulk" and lists separations rising 19.2, 21.4, 24.3, 25.1 cm-1.
It assigns "B = 1L (Δ 19.2 cm-1), A = 2L (21.4)" and says "A, B and the 1L/2L split are robust."
It gives "D = about 4L (24.3...)" and "C = bulk-like (25.1...)", says "Δ saturates here, so 4L to roughly 6L cannot be distinguished", and adds "Layer numbers above 4L... cannot be fixed."

It warns that intensity is "strongly affected by interference in the 285 nm SiO2" and "should not be used to count layers", but it never mentions the rise to about 4L and then fall, or that a monolayer can be stronger than bulk, and it claims a monotonic Si-normalised trend.

It says the roughly 1 cm-1 differences are comparable to "strain, doping and substrate effects" and that "a doping contribution of about 1 cm-1 cannot be excluded", but it gives no strain coefficient (about 4.5 cm-1/%) and does not say that electron doping softens and broadens A1g.
It reports A1g FWHM of 6.16 (A, "the broadest", matching "A1g widening toward 2L"), 4.75 (B) and 4.45 (D), against 2.86 cm-1 for bulk-like C, and says "The E2g1 width is constant (2.0–2.1 cm-1)."
It uses the Si line for calibration ("spectrometer reads about 0.7 cm-1 low", "--si-correct") and asks "Were the Si line and the laser line calibrated...?"

wrong_claims.why: Layers are assigned from Δ, and intensity is called "not an independent thickness measure."
It correctly states that E2g1 softens and the separation grows with thickness.
It says "Flake C has one cosmic-ray spike at 265.1 cm-1, which was removed."

items.why: The report says "The ~352 cm-1 band is an unresolved doublet of 2LA(M) and E2g1", fits two Lorentzians and gets "2LA(M) 351.12" and "E2g1 355.30" for spot 1.

Spot 1 matches ("2LA(M)/A1g fitted height ratio ~2.35"), but for spot 2 the report gives only an area ratio of "≈ 0.9", not about 0.5, and the summary confusingly says 2LA(M) is "strongly enhanced at spot 2".
The report states "A1g is 417.28 cm-1 at spot 1 and 420.08 cm-1 at spot 2 (+2.8 cm-1 stiffening)", matching the 1L and bulk reference values.
The report gives "Δ = 61.98 cm-1" for spot 1 and "Δ = 64.70 cm-1" for spot 2, computed after the doublet was fitted as two components.
The report notes "3L and bulk cannot be separated by Δ (64.6 vs 64.8)", cites a 1L-2L gap of only 1.4 cm-1 and A1g reference steps of about 1 cm-1, and assigns spot 2 only as "≥3L".
The report checks calibration against the Si line ("Si offsets +0.21 and +0.09 cm-1 differ by only 0.12 cm-1") and says the 514.5 nm resonance controls the 2LA(M) intensity.

wrong_claims.why: The report rejects the single-peak approach explicitly: "Using the merged ~351.7/353.1 cm-1 peak as E2g gives Δ = 65.6 ... That is wrong for spot 1".
The report treats 2LA(M) as a resonant second-order mode, and it says LA(M) "is not a defect marker".
